title: 공명 측정자 — 광역 rule-set (16 rules × 4 Wolfram classes)
question: is basin↔Φ correlation rule-CLASS-dependent? does class IV (complex) reproduce H_346's +0.55, while class III (chaotic) collapses?

rule_set.selection_rationale: 4 rules per Wolfram class, committed in source BEFORE measurement; broader than BENCH#1's 8 mixed rules

class_averaged.note: mean of 4 per-class r values (df=2 each, n_rules_per_class=4)

verdict_rule_preregistered.PASS_class_iv_only: class IV r ≥ +0.5 AND class III r near 0 → 🟢 H_345/346 narrow scope confirmed
verdict_rule_preregistered.PASS_broader_robust: class IV r ≥ +0.5 AND class III r ≥ +0.5 → 🟢 broader robustness (unexpected)
verdict_rule_preregistered.FAIL_falsified: class-avg |r| < 0.2 for BOTH signals → 🔴 capstone falsified

verdict_text: Class IV max_basin↔Φ = 0.0 (degenerate: all class-IV rules tested have max_basin=4 — basin axis is constant within class IV, no variance to correlate). Class III max_basin↔Φ = −0.97 (strongly REVERSED from H_346's +0.55). Overall 16-rule max_basin↔Φ = −0.90 (strongly REVERSED). H_346 capstone's '+0.55 max_basin↔Φ' is a rule-set curation artifact — it does NOT survive class-systematic broadening. HOWEVER: n_attr↔Φ retains a strong-magnitude signal per class (|r| > 0.6 in 3 of 4 classes), with sign DIFFERING by class (II/III positive, I positive, IV negative). The H_346 n_attr↔Φ = −0.951 specifically reflects the class IV regime (canonical 4 rules {110,30,105,150} include rule 110 ∈ class IV).
key_findings: OVERALL max_basin↔Φ = −0.896 (16 rules, n=4) — strong reversal vs H_346's +0.550 confirms BENCH#1's WEAK-REVERSED finding at higher n_rules + better Wolfram-class coverage

class IV max_basin↔Φ degenerate (r=0): all 4 tested class IV rules have max_basin=4. Within class IV, basin-axis variance vanishes — basin↔Φ is structurally unmeasurable here. n_attr↔Φ = −0.998 (matches H_346 sign, very strong)
class III chaotic max_basin↔Φ = −0.968 (rule 90 outlier driver — additive XOR Φ=0 at max basin=16)
class I fixed max_basin↔Φ = −0.600 (rules 0/8 have flat fields → low Φ at max basin)
class II periodic max_basin↔Φ = −0.920 (period-collapse rules drag Φ down at high basin)
n_attr↔Φ SIGN SWITCHES by class: I/II/III positive (more attractors → higher Φ) vs IV negative (more attractors → lower Φ, matches H_346)

H_346 canonical 4 rules {110, 30, 105, 150}: 110 ∈ class IV, 30/105 ∈ class III, 150 ∈ class III. The +0.55 emerges from a class III/IV mix where H_346's specific 4 rules' max_basin happens to anti-correlate with their n_attr
h_345_346_scope_refinement: H_345/346 capstone's '+0.55 max_basin↔Φ' is RULE-SET-CURATION-DEPENDENT. The robust finding across class-systematic broadening (16 rules, 4 classes × 4 rules) is the |n_attr↔Φ| coupling (always > 0.6 in 3/4 classes), NOT max_basin↔Φ (which depends on which class IV / class III rules are included). Recommended H_345/346 scope correction: 'n_attr↔Φ coupling is robust in magnitude per Wolfram class; max_basin↔Φ +sign in H_346 reflects the curated 4-rule frame, not a class-systematic regularity.'
honest_caveats: n_rules_per_class=4 → df=2 per class, so per-class r ≥ 0.95 is borderline (3-point fit can hit |r| ≈ 1 by chance). Replication at 8 rules per class (df=6) needed for class-resolved certainty
class IV has only 2 canonical rules in the literature (54, 110); rules 124, 137 are quasi-class-IV per Wolfram's Atlas; tested set max_basin all = 4, a degenerate axis for that class
n=4 limits sys_state count to 16 (vs n=5 = 32); class-resolved follow-up at n=5 needed to separate n axis from rule-set axis
rule 90 (additive XOR) is again a class III outlier (max_basin=16, Φ=0); class III r=−0.97 is partially carried by this outlier as in BENCH#1
df=2 in class-averaged r-of-r is not a standard inference (treating per-class r as samples); reported as descriptive heuristic only
the verdict label uses pre-registered tiers; the diagnostic refinement (class-IV degenerate basin axis) is post-hoc but explicitly flagged
anti_tautology: rule list committed BEFORE measurement in source (4 rules per class)
Wolfram class assignments follow Wolfram (2002) / Wuensche-Lesser atlas — not tuned post-hoc
basin/Φ independently computed (dynamics vs TPM structure)
pre-registered verdict thresholds honored even though primary axis is degenerate in class IV
all 16 measurements reported verbatim including outliers and degenerate class IV basins
follow_ups: 8 rules per class (32 rules total, df=6 per class) — to remove the df=2 borderline issue
n=5 + 16-rule bench → separate n axis from rule-set axis (class IV basin variance also expected to grow with n)
drop rule 90 from class III and replace with another non-additive class III rule (122, 146) — test whether the −0.97 class III r survives outlier removal
investigate why class IV rules 54/110/124/137 all have max_basin=4 at n=4 — is this a small-n degeneracy or a class IV signature?
